title: Jellyfish the Weight of Sumo Wrestlers Sank a 10-Ton Fishing Boat

scenes.text: A fishing boat sank. The culprit had no brain.
November 2009, off Chiba, Japan. The Diasan Shinsho-maru, a 10-ton trawler, hauls in its net on a calm sea under clear skies.
Inside the net: dozens of Nomura's jellyfish. Each one up to two metres across and 200 kilograms, the weight of a sumo wrestler.
The weight tipped the boat over. All three crew were thrown into the water and picked up by another trawler nearby.
In bad bloom years, these jellyfish clog nets across the region. In 2005, some fishermen in northern Japan lost 80 percent of their income.
No brain, no bones, no teeth. Just enough of them to sink a boat.

description:
In November 2009 the Diasan Shinsho-maru, a 10-ton Japanese trawler, capsized off Chiba while hauling in a net full of Nomura's jellyfish; its three crew were rescued by another boat.
Nomura's jellyfish can reach two metres across and about 200 kilograms, and in bloom years they have cost Japanese fisheries a large share of their income.
Would you keep fishing in jellyfish season?
subject: Nomura's jellyfish
first_comment: A single Nomura's jellyfish can weigh as much as a sumo wrestler. What is the strangest thing you have ever pulled up in a net?
